messages:
Maya: Kicking off the staged migration tonight during the 02:00 UTC change window. Sequence: US -> EU -> APAC. Goal is to keep user-impact <1% and to avoid cache thrash. Warm pool plan: reserve ~12 nodes per region (roughly 10% traffic) and a 20% quota cushion. Sam pls confirm EU dedicated pin and any billing alerts. @deploy-bot will manage slice transitions.
Sam: Confirmed — I'm pinning eu-dedicated to v4.3.1 for the rollout window. I'll also suspend noncritical background jobs in EU for the next 90m. Billing alerts: set to notify at 80% of commit.
deploy-bot: rollout job 2120003456 created by Maya. Stages queued: us-1 (started), eu-1 (hold), apac-1 (hold). Canary traffic=2% -> ramp to 10% per stage if health OK.
Oliver: Quick capacity snapshot before we start ramping. Ran the check against the capacity API:
```
# capacity-check --region eu
available_gpus: 28
reserved_warm_pool: 12
current_utilization: 61%
possible_burst_capacity: 40
```
We have a ~20% runway versus target traffic. Looks OK but keep an eye on p95.
Carla: Deployed canary to us-1, initial metrics look fine. p95 latency stable, error rate 0.1%. Moving to scheduled ramp to 10% for US in 10m.
Ryan: FYI I updated the release notes doc with the network changes and the feature flags: https://internal/release-notes/2026-03-20-v4.3.1 (edit perms set).
deploy-bot: us-1 ramp to 10% complete. Health checks: pass=98/100, errors=2. Rolling traffic forward to eu-1 canary.
Carla: Starting eu-1 canary at 2%. Observability: p50 fine, p95 trending up. Posting quick snapshot:
```
region: eu-1
canary_traffic: 2%
p95_latency_before: 320ms
p95_latency_now: 370ms
cpu_pressure: 78%
kv_cache_miss: +4%
```
Can we hold on ramping to 10% until we confirm cache warmup?
Maya: Hold eu-1 ramp. Increase warm pool by 3 nodes for eu-1 and re-run prefix cache warmup job (Ryan can trigger). We want to avoid user-facing latency spikes.
Ryan: Triggering cache warmup job now -> job id cw-2120003456-1. ETA 3m.
Oliver: Noted a spike in GPU queue latency for eu-1 at ~02:15 UTC when canary hit 2%. Investigating. Quick check shows spot preemption rate for the zone is slightly higher than baseline (0.6% vs 0.2%). That could explain jitter.
Carla: After warmup and extra warm-pool nodes p95 dropped to 335ms but still ~5% above baseline. I'm seeing CPU pressure at 92% on one host; it's the one owning the KV hot-shard. Propose we rollback eu-1 to v4.2.9 until we can migrate the hot-shard and increase warm pool to 15%.
Sam: Agreed with conservative move. Initiating rollback eu-1 -> v4.2.9 and pin to v4.2.9 for the next 60m. Notifying billing and customer success.
deploy-bot: rollback job rb-2120003456-eu started. Rolling traffic from v4.3.1 -> v4.2.9 for slice eu-1. Expected completion ~2m.
deploy-bot: rollback job rb-2120003456-eu completed. eu-1 now pinned to v4.2.9. Health checks: pass=95/100, errors=5. Reopening canary hold for re-assessment.
Maya: Good catch. Notes for post-mortem: hot-shard migration, improve pre-deploy cache warmup (make it region-aware), and make warm pool adjustments automatic when preemption >0.4%.
Oliver: I'll open a short follow-up DR to tune autoscaler thresholds and add a small playbook snippet: if spot_preempt_rate >0.4% then increase warm_pool +10%.
Carla: OK — monitoring EU for 30m. If stable, we'll reattempt a smaller canary (5%) with extra warm nodes and a KV shard handoff out-of-band.
Sam: I'll update the release notes and the rollout doc to reflect the temporary pin and the rollback rationale. Everyone: please add any brief observations to the thread before we close the window.
Maya: Thanks all — good noisy-but-safe rollout. Closing the loop once EU is green for 30m, then we'll re-evaluate APAC timing. :thumbsup:
